title: Slime Mold
description: A Physarum polycephalum plasmodium grown from an agent model: tens of thousands of virtual protoplasm streams each sniff the trail ahead (left / centre / right), steer toward the strongest scent and lay their own trail, which diffuses and evaporates. Inoculated at the centre, the colonised region breathes — it advances outward as a fan (a fine green foraging mesh sweeping the margin with a dense reticulated vein web consolidating behind it), then pulls back in as the abandoned outer web is left unfed and fades, then grows again, never settling. A vein-sharpening feedback pulls flux into the strong routes so thick golden transport trunks radiate from the source and taper to fine twigs, and the render lights it as a real plasmodium: green at the advancing mesh, gold along the tubes, a wet cream sheen down the biggest trunks, all glowing over dark agar; beats surge the growth outward. Click to drop an oat flake the colony reaches toward and consumes. Grow, recede, density, sensing, vein sharpening, sheen and glow are all live and audio-mappable.
